title: FAIR-RAG: Faithful Adaptive Iterative Refinement for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

novelty.problem: Existing RAG frameworks struggle with complex, multi-hop queries and often fail to comprehensively gather and synthesize information from disparate sources.
novelty.new_contribution: Introduction of FAIR-RAG, a novel framework that uses an Iterative Refinement Cycle and Structured Evidence Assessment (SEA) to systematically identify and fill evidence gaps.
novelty.architecture_innovation: The SEA module deconstructs the initial query into a checklist of required findings, audits the aggregated evidence, and identifies informational gaps, which are then used to generate targeted sub-queries.
novelty.results: FAIR-RAG significantly outperforms strong baselines on challenging multi-hop QA benchmarks, achieving an F1-score of 0.453 on HotpotQA, an absolute improvement of 8.3 points over the strongest iterative baseline.
novelty.why_interesting: FAIR-RAG introduces a structured and evidence-driven approach to RAG, which is crucial for handling complex, multi-hop queries and ensuring comprehensive and accurate information synthesis.

title: Speech Retrieval-Augmented Generation without Automatic Speech Recognition

novelty.problem: ASR errors propagating to retrieval and generation steps in question answering over speech data.
novelty.new_contribution: Introduction of SpeechRAG, a framework for open-question answering over spoken data that bypasses ASR by directly retrieving audio passages from text-based queries.
novelty.architecture_innovation: Fine-tuning a pre-trained speech encoder into a speech adapter fed into a frozen LLM-based retrieval model, aligning the embedding spaces of text and speech.
novelty.results: Retrieval experiments show that direct speech retrieval does not degrade over the text-based baseline and outperforms cascaded systems using ASR. For generation, the approach outperforms cascaded text-based models when there is high WER in the transcripts.
novelty.why_interesting: SpeechRAG addresses a significant limitation in cascaded ASR-based systems by directly handling speech, which can lead to more accurate and robust question answering over spoken data.

title: HM-RAG: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation

novelty.problem: Complex queries in RAG systems require coordinated reasoning across heterogeneous data ecosystems, which single-agent RAG systems struggle to handle.
novelty.new_contribution: HM-RAG, a hierarchical multi-agent multimodal RAG framework that enhances query understanding and accuracy by integrating textual, graph-relational, and web-derived evidence.
novelty.architecture_innovation: Three-tiered architecture with specialized agents: Decomposition Agent, Multi-source Retrieval Agents, and Decision Agent, enabling modular and coordinated reasoning.
novelty.results: 12.95% improvement in answer accuracy and 3.56% boost in question classification accuracy over baseline RAG systems on ScienceQA and CrisisMMD benchmarks. State-of-the-art results in zero-shot settings on both datasets.
novelty.why_interesting: HM-RAG addresses the limitations of single-agent RAG systems by introducing a modular and hierarchical architecture, significantly improving performance on complex queries and establishing new benchmarks in zero-shot settings.

title: Omni-Router: Sharing Routing Decisions in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts for Speech Recognition

novelty.problem: Improving the efficiency and performance of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures in automatic speech recognition (ASR).
novelty.new_contribution: Introduction of the Omni-router Transformer, which uses a shared router across different MoE layers to increase cooperation and specialization among experts.
novelty.architecture_innovation: Shared router mechanism across multiple MoE layers to enhance inter-layer correlation and expert specialization.
novelty.results: Achieved lower training loss and consistently outperformed dense and Switch Transformer models, reducing average word error rates by 11.2% and 8.2%, respectively, across 10 diverse ASR benchmarks.
novelty.why_interesting: The Omni-router Transformer introduces a novel approach to sharing routing decisions, which could lead to more efficient and robust ASR models. The significant reduction in word error rates across diverse benchmarks is particularly noteworthy.

title: Mixture-of-Experts Knowledge Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Multi-Agent LLM-based Recommendation

novelty.problem: LLM-based recommender systems suffer from outdated knowledge and ineffective knowledge graph retrieval-augmented generation (KG-RAG) due to one-size-fits-all retrieval strategies and structural information loss.
novelty.new_contribution: Proposes MixRAGRec, a cooperative multi-agent framework that addresses the challenges of query complexity and retrieval granularity in KG-RAG for recommendations.
novelty.architecture_innovation: Integrates a Mixture-of-Experts Retrieval Agent, a Knowledge Preference Alignment Agent, and a Contrastive Learning-reinforced Recommendation Agent, trained with Mixture-of-Experts Multi-Agent Policy Optimization (MMAPO).
novelty.results: Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework.
novelty.why_interesting: MixRAGRec addresses key challenges in KG-RAG for recommendations, such as query complexity and retrieval granularity, using a novel multi-agent framework. This could significantly improve the performance and relevance of LLM-based recommender systems.

title: Agent-UniRAG: A Trainable Open-Source LLM Agent Framework for Unified Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems

novelty.problem: Unified retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems for complex reasoning tasks, including both single-hop and multi-hop queries.
novelty.new_contribution: A trainable agent framework called Agent-UniRAG that unifies single-hop and multi-hop RAG tasks in an end-to-end manner.
novelty.architecture_innovation: Designs an LLM agent framework to solve RAG tasks step-by-step, enhancing interpretability and effectiveness.
novelty.results: Comparable performances with closed-source and larger open-source LLMs across various RAG benchmarks.
novelty.why_interesting: Agent-UniRAG addresses the gap in unified RAG systems, making it more applicable to real-world scenarios. The availability of the code and synthetic dataset further enhances its practical value.

title: Toward Low-Latency End-to-End Voice Agents for Telecommunications Using Streaming ASR, Quantized LLMs, and Real-Time TTS

novelty.problem: Developing a low-latency, domain-specific AI voice agent pipeline for real-time telecommunications applications such as call center automation and customer support.
novelty.new_contribution: A specialized pipeline integrating streaming ASR, a 4-bit quantized LLM, a domain-specific embedding model, and real-time TTS, all tailored for the telecom domain.
novelty.architecture_innovation: The use of 4-bit quantization for the LLM (TSLAM) to reduce latency, and the integration of domain-specific models (T-VEC, TTE, T-Synth) to enhance relevance and performance in telecom applications.
novelty.results: The system achieves real-time factors (RTF) below 1.0 for TSLAM, TTE, and T-Synth, demonstrating low latency suitable for enterprise telecom deployments. Evaluated on a dataset of 500 human-recorded telecom questions, the system shows strong performance in latency, domain relevance, and real-time capabilities.
novelty.why_interesting: The combination of domain-specific models and 4-bit quantization for low-latency performance is a significant advancement for real-time telecom applications. The system's ability to handle complex telecom queries with high relevance and low latency makes it highly relevant for industry use.

title: MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation

novelty.problem: LLMs often generate outdated or incorrect information, and existing RAG systems struggle with the quality of retrieved documents, leading to performance degradation and increased computational overhead.
novelty.new_contribution: Introduction of MAIN-RAG, a training-free RAG framework that uses multiple LLM agents to collaboratively filter and score retrieved documents, improving the quality and relevance of the information used.
novelty.architecture_innovation: Adaptive filtering mechanism that dynamically adjusts the relevance filtering threshold based on score distributions, and inter-agent consensus for robust document selection.
novelty.results: MAIN-RAG outperforms traditional RAG approaches on four QA benchmarks, achieving a 2-11% improvement in answer accuracy and reducing the number of irrelevant retrieved documents.
novelty.why_interesting: MAIN-RAG addresses a critical issue in RAG systems by improving the quality of retrieved documents without additional training, making it a practical and effective solution for enhancing LLM performance.

title: MASS-RAG: Multi-Agent Synthesis Retrieval-Augmented Generation

novelty.problem: Improving retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in the presence of noisy, incomplete, or heterogeneous retrieved contexts.
novelty.new_contribution: Introduction of MASS-RAG, a multi-agent synthesis approach that uses role-specialized agents for evidence summarization, extraction, and reasoning.
novelty.architecture_innovation: A multi-agent architecture with distinct roles for processing retrieved information and a synthesis stage to combine their outputs.
novelty.results: Experiments on four benchmarks show consistent improvements over strong RAG baselines, especially in scenarios with distributed relevant evidence.
novelty.why_interesting: MASS-RAG addresses a significant challenge in RAG by leveraging a multi-agent system, which could enhance the robustness and accuracy of information retrieval and generation tasks.

title: A Collaborative Multi-Agent Approach to Retrieval-Augmented Generation Across Diverse Data

novelty.problem: Traditional RAG systems are inefficient and less accurate when dealing with diverse data sources such as relational databases, document stores, and graph databases.
novelty.new_contribution: A multi-agent RAG system where specialized agents handle query generation for different data sources, improving efficiency and accuracy.
novelty.architecture_innovation: Modular framework with specialized agents for relational, NoSQL, and document-based systems, collaborating within a distributed environment.
novelty.results: Not reported
novelty.why_interesting: The multi-agent approach addresses the limitations of single-agent RAG systems, making it more suitable for complex, heterogeneous data environments. This could significantly enhance the performance and scalability of generative AI applications.

title: GEC-RAG: Improving Generative Error Correction via Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Automatic Speech Recognition Systems

novelty.problem: High Word Error Rates (WER) in ASR systems for low-resource languages and specific domains.
novelty.new_contribution: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach called GEC-RAG to improve ASR accuracy in low-resource domains like Persian.
novelty.architecture_innovation: Uses a knowledge base of ASR predictions and ground truths, retrieves lexically similar examples using TF-IDF, and feeds these to a Generative LLM for targeted corrections.
novelty.results: Significantly reduces WER in Persian, demonstrating potential for domain adaptation and low-resource scenarios.
novelty.why_interesting: The approach leverages existing ASR systems without requiring direct modification, making it adaptable to various domains by updating the knowledge base.

title: Speech Encoder Fusion for LLM-based Automatic Speech Recognition

novelty.problem: Improving ASR performance by leveraging multiple pre-trained speech encoders in LLM-based systems.
novelty.new_contribution: Investigation of fusion strategies for combining multiple pre-trained speech encoders to enhance speech-aware LLMs for ASR.
novelty.architecture_innovation: Explores learned combinations and Transformer-based fusion architectures beyond simple feature concatenation.
novelty.results: Fusing multiple speech encoders improves ASR performance in mono- and multilingual settings as well as diarized speech recognition with minimal computational overhead.
novelty.why_interesting: The paper addresses the practical challenge of leveraging multiple encoders to improve ASR, which could lead to more robust and versatile speech recognition systems.

title: LA-RAG:Enhancing LLM-based ASR Accuracy with Retrieval-Augmented Generation

novelty.problem: Improving ASR accuracy in LLMs, particularly under varied acoustic conditions and accents.
novelty.new_contribution: Introduction of LA-RAG, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation paradigm that leverages fine-grained token-level speech datastores and a speech-to-speech retrieval mechanism.
novelty.architecture_innovation: Combines LLM in-context learning (ICL) with a retrieval mechanism to enhance ASR accuracy.
novelty.results: Significant improvements in ASR accuracy on Mandarin and various Chinese dialect datasets, especially in handling accent variations.
novelty.why_interesting: LA-RAG addresses a critical issue in ASR by improving accuracy in challenging acoustic conditions, which is particularly relevant for multilingual and dialectal speech recognition.

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) for Fintech: Agentic Design and Evaluation

novelty.problem: Specialized domains like fintech pose challenges for RAG systems due to domain-specific ontologies, dense terminology, and acronyms.
novelty.new_contribution: An agentic RAG architecture with a modular pipeline of specialized agents for query reformulation, sub-query decomposition, acronym resolution, and context re-ranking.
novelty.architecture_innovation: Modular pipeline of specialized agents including intelligent query reformulation, iterative sub-query decomposition, contextual acronym resolution, and cross-encoder-based context re-ranking.
novelty.results: The agentic RAG system outperforms the baseline in retrieval precision and relevance, but with increased latency.
novelty.why_interesting: The modular approach with specialized agents addresses specific challenges in fintech, demonstrating improved performance in retrieval precision and relevance.

title: On the Problem of Text-To-Speech Model Selection for Synthetic Data Generation in Automatic Speech Recognition

novelty.problem: Selecting the most effective TTS models for generating synthetic data to train ASR systems.
novelty.new_contribution: Comparison of five TTS decoder architectures for synthetic data generation and their impact on CTC-based ASR training.
novelty.architecture_innovation: Not reported
novelty.results: Auto-regressive decoding outperforms non-autoregressive decoding for synthetic data generation. No clear relationship found between computable metrics (NISQA MOS, intelligibility) and ASR performance.
novelty.why_interesting: The study provides insights into the selection of TTS models for synthetic data generation, which is crucial for improving ASR systems. It highlights the importance of auto-regressive decoding and the lack of clear correlations between common metrics and ASR performance.

title: AgentWorld: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Collaboration of Multi-agent LLMs

novelty.problem: Evaluating long-horizon, multi-agent collaboration in LLM-based agents
novelty.new_contribution: Introduction of AgentWorld, a benchmark with 100 human-annotated tasks and 100 augmented variants for evaluating long-horizon collaboration in a MMORPG sandbox
novelty.architecture_innovation: Causal Collaboration Effectiveness (CCE), a graph-based metric to measure the effectiveness of collaboration
novelty.results: Best model (DeepSeek R1-70B) achieves 52.0% task success, with common failure modes including communication breakdowns, role confusion, and inability to maintain shared plans
novelty.why_interesting: AgentWorld addresses a significant gap in evaluating multi-agent collaboration, particularly in long-horizon tasks, and introduces a novel metric to quantify collaboration effectiveness.

title: DeepEdu-v1: Efficient and Scalable Agentic LLMs for Vietnamese Education

novelty.problem: Improving AI tutoring for Vietnamese education while addressing data sovereignty and local content accuracy issues.
novelty.new_contribution: Introduction of DeepEdu-v1, an AI-tutoring system that addresses the limitations of cloud assistants and self-hosted models in Vietnamese education.
novelty.architecture_innovation: Two key innovations: a long-context inference engine that reduces retrieval calls and prefill latency, and a self-improving agentic layer that curates a verified playbook from past interactions.
novelty.results: Achieves nearly x2 TTFT speedup over standard vLLM serving and lifts agentic accuracy from 70.0% to 79.5% on complex tasks, with significant gains in financial-reasoning and interactive-agent benchmarks.
novelty.why_interesting: DeepEdu-v1 addresses critical issues in AI tutoring for developing regions, offering a scalable and culturally relevant solution that enhances both performance and accuracy.

title: Structured Reasoning Agentic Framework for Interpretable Critical View of Safety Assessment

novelty.problem: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy is challenging due to the complex anatomy of the hepatocystic triangle and the risk of bile duct injury. Existing methods for Critical View of Safety (CVS) assessment lack interpretability and compositional generalization.
novelty.new_contribution: Proposes ReasonCVS, a structured reasoning agentic framework that decomposes CVS assessment into explicit, fine-grained anatomical verification using Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and a Rationale-Aware Reasoning Agent.
novelty.architecture_innovation: Introduces an Anatomical Scene Graph Abstraction (ASGA) and a Rationale-Aware Reasoning Agent, which uses a Large Language Model (LLM) fine-tuned via rationale distillation to evaluate individual sub-criteria and synthesize a final verdict with a traceable clinical rationale.
novelty.results: Achieves superior performance (68.1% mAP) on the Endoscapes-CVS201 benchmark compared to state-of-the-art methods, while providing interpretable, criterion-level explanations.
novelty.why_interesting: The framework combines VLMs and LLMs in a novel way to enhance interpretability and reliability in surgical scene understanding, which is crucial for improving patient safety.

title: EAServe: Encode-Aware Disaggregated Serving for Multimodal Large Language Models

novelty.problem: Resource allocation and utilization challenges in serving multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with a three-stage Encode-Prefill-Decode (EPD) pipeline.
novelty.new_contribution: EAServe, a system that optimizes the EPD pipeline by managing load-adaptive micro-batching, rate-controlled partial offload, and dynamic GPU partitioning.
novelty.architecture_innovation: Repositions the Encode stage as the control point of the EPD pipeline, integrating it with Prefill and Decode stages to improve resource utilization and performance.
novelty.results: EAServe delivers up to 4.3x and 1.7x higher goodput than NVIDIA Dynamo and vLLM, respectively, under identical SLO constraints, and achieves more balanced and higher GPU utilization.
novelty.why_interesting: EAServe addresses a critical bottleneck in serving MLLMs by optimizing the EPD pipeline, leading to significant performance improvements and better resource utilization.

title: SatNav: A Scalable Benchmark for Long-Horizon UAV Vision-Language Navigation from Satellite Imagery

novelty.problem: Scaling existing benchmarks for urban UAV vision-language navigation (VLN) is limited by the reliance on costly 3D assets, reducing geographic diversity and episode scale.
novelty.new_contribution: Introduction of SatNav, a scalable long-horizon UAV VLN benchmark using high-resolution satellite imagery, with 118K episodes from 59 scenes across 18 cities.
novelty.architecture_innovation: SwiftVLN, a modular framework with switchable memory components for systematic memory-design ablations.
novelty.results: Benchmarking shows that city-scale navigation remains challenging for both classical VLN agents and recent LVLMs. Satellite-trained models can transfer to real-flight UAV observations.
novelty.why_interesting: SatNav addresses the scalability issue in UAV VLN benchmarks and introduces a practical framework for long-horizon navigation tasks. The ability to transfer satellite-trained models to real UAVs is particularly noteworthy.
